mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary stance, raising discount rates and reducing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a rise in housing starts (HOUST) above their 12-month moving average signals weakening aggregate demand but a constructive housing cycle, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as sector rotation benefits industrials and materials.
regime_hint: late-cycle demand softening with sector resilience
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered instances, or the average return is not statistically distinguishable from a flat baseline.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 5.5% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing corporate earnings expectations and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) below its 6-month moving average for four consecutive months signals a contraction in manufacturing activity, which historically precedes negative equity returns over the next 60 trading days due to earnings downgrades.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not statistically different from zero.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month decline in the federal funds rate below 2% signals an emergency easing episode, which typically boosts risk assets and results in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS drops below 2% in one month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically above zero.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in real personal savings (RSAFS) and a fall in personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) by more than 1 standard deviation within the same month signals a precautionary savings regime, which historically precedes muted equity returns over the next 20 trading days as consumers delay discretionary spending.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > +1σ AND GDPC1 < -1σ in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not statistically different from zero.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid acceleration in payroll employment growth (PAYEMS) above 300,000 new jobs per month for two consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which typically precedes positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to higher wage and profit expectations.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically above zero.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated increase in both housing starts (HOUST) and industrial production (INDPRO) above their respective 12-month moving averages for two consecutive months signals a broad-based recovery in demand and supply, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12-month MA AND INDPRO > 12-month MA for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not statistically above zero.
